source.title: Climber: Toward Efficient Scaling Laws for Large Recommendation Models
source.authors: Songpei Xu; Shi-Jia Wang; Da Guo; Xianwen Guo; Qiang Xiao; Bin Huang; Guanlin Wu; Chuan-Jiang Luo

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures recommendation-model performance as sequence length, layer count, and compute are scaled. This extends scaling experiments to recommendation models and recommendation metrics, not language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports recommendation AUC curves and online recommendation-metric changes, not held-out language-model cross-entropy. It does not sweep language-model parameters or training tokens. The equivalent-FLOPs table varies recommendation-model sequence length and layer count; it does not measure the parameter/token allocation specified in V3. The paper also reports architectural ablations and baseline comparisons, which are not included as scaling-law results.
record.test_reason: The study scales a recommendation model (Climber) along layer count, sequence length and FLOPs and reports offline AUC curves. It describes the curves as power-law-like, which bears on V5 in a new domain. The evidence is qualitative: figures only, AUC rather than loss, and no fitted exponents.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Climber has a more efficient AUC-vs-FLOPs scaling curve than Transformer and DLRM in recommendation. They find that sequence length and depth should be scaled jointly (alternating online), and that online metrics scale with FLOPs, reaching +12.19%. They also credit acceleration techniques for enabling 100× more complex models at the same serving cost.
record.recipe_differences: Recommendation-model experiments use AUC and an online recommendation metric, scaling sequence length and layer count rather than language-model parameter/token counts and held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The recommendation-model AUC varies with the sequence-length/layer-count combination at equivalent FLOPs; the reported online metric also differs across model configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed FLOPs (C ∝ s·l), the sequence-length/layer split changes AUC by up to ~1%. The balanced split is best at each budget (e.g. 400s×4l 0.8301; 800s×8l 0.8382).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In recommendation models, the allocation of compute between input sequence length and depth at fixed FLOPs affects AUC, with balanced allocation best.

fits_no_version.finding: The online A/B metric relative to DLRM rises with Climber FLOPs from −4.95% at 1× to +12.19% at 620×. It is not strictly ordered by FLOPs: the 397× configuration gave +10.68% and the 479× configuration +7.78%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online recommendation metrics improve roughly monotonically with model FLOPs, with configuration (depth vs. sequence length) mattering beyond FLOPs.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’25)
record.problems: The scaling curves are primarily presented as plots without numerical values or fitted exponents in the text. The reported scaling outcomes are recommendation AUC and online metrics, not held-out language-model loss. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for these results. Its FLOPs analysis uses C ∝ s ∗ l and focuses on the linear sequence-length component.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported scaling curves, equivalent-FLOPs allocation table, or online scaling table. Table 2 model comparisons and component ablations are not included because they do not directly report the scaling results captured here.

untested.parts: Image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. No fitted power-law exponent or goodness of fit, and no loss-based measure (LogLoss scaling is not plotted).
Not tested: no small-run fits used to predict larger runs (Fig 1a's DLRM extrapolation line is not evaluated).
Not tested: the fixed-FLOPs split is sequence length × layers, not parameters × tokens.
Not tested: no LM downstream tasks.

missing.what: AUC-vs-FLOPs scaling curves for DLRM, Transformer and Climber. These show Climber with a higher intercept and slope, and crossover points with DLRM at ~10^7.5 FLOPs (Climber) and ~10^8.2 (Transformer, Fig 1a).
Climber-large (12 layers, 800 sequence length) versus Climber (2 layers, 200 sequence length): AUC gains with scale on four datasets (e.g. industrial 0.8230→0.8398; Spotify 0.7663→0.7702).

record.verdict_notes: V6 was moved off the online rows: those rows compare against a different baseline model and are not LM downstream performance. The 'reversed' states were an artefact of the DLRM baseline. FLOPs are defined crudely as C ∝ s·l, ignoring quadratic attention cost. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss, parameter-count or training-token sweeps.
No small-run fits or predictions of much larger language-model losses.
The study compares recommendation-model layer count and sequence length at fixed FLOPs, not parameter and token counts or stable powers of compute.
It does not test how depth, width or other architecture details affect language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests recommendation models and AUC scaling only; does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
Tests recommendation AUC and an online recommendation metric as the recommendation model is scaled; does not test language-model downstream tasks or prediction from pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents or alternative fitting choices are reported; the fixed-FLOPs comparison does not test the stated parameter/token allocation law.

relationships.condition: Climber recommendation model, industrial dataset, offline AUC versus layer number (sequence length fixed) and versus sequence length (layers fixed)
relationships.reason: Authors state AUC improves 'in a manner similar to a power-law' with scale. This is qualitative and figure-only, with no exponent (r12, r13).
relationships.display_finding: AUC improved with more layers or longer sequences in a pattern described as resembling a power law, without an estimated exponent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Climber AUC when layer count or sequence length is increased with the other held fixed
reader_labels.reason: The text describes both curves as improving in a manner similar to a power law; this is qualitative evidence in a recommendation setting, not a language-model loss result (r12, r13).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Larger Climber configurations in the online recommendation test
reader_labels.reason: The configurations from 4.11 × 10^8 through 3.61 × 10^9 FLOPs report positive online metric improvements over DLRM (r17–r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Smaller Climber configurations in the online recommendation test
reader_labels.reason: The three lower-FLOPs configurations report negative online metric changes versus DLRM, and the gains are not strictly ordered by FLOPs across configurations (r14–r16, r19–r20).
